{{Notability|Organizations|date=December 2025}}
{{Short description|Non-profit organization dedicated to number theory}}
The '''Number Theory Foundation''' ('''NTF''') is a [[non-profit]] organization based in the [[United States]] which supports research and conferences in the field of [[number theory]], with a particular focus on computational aspects and explicit methods.{{r|ntf}}

The NTF funds the [[Selfridge prize]] awarded at each [[ANTS (conference)|Algorithmic Number Theory Symposium  (ANTS)]]{{r|antsxii}}{{r|antsxiii}} and is a regular supporter of several conferences and organizations in number theory, including the [[Canadian Number Theory Association|Canadian Number Theory Association (CNTA)]],{{r|cntaxiv}}{{r|cntaxv}} Women in Numbers (WIN), and the [[West Coast Number Theory|West Coast Number Theory (WCNT)]] conference.{{r|ntf}}

==History==
The NTF was created in 1999 via a grant from [[John Selfridge]] with an initial board of directors including [[Paul Bateman]], [[John Brillhart]], Richard Blecksmith, [[Brian Conrey]], [[Ronald Graham]], [[Richard K. Guy|Richard Guy]], [[Carl Pomerance]], John Selfridge, [[Samuel S. Wagstaff Jr.|Sam Wagstaff]], and [[Hugh C. Williams|Hugh Williams]].{{r|niu}}{{r|mathtimes}}  Carl Pomerance served as President of the foundation for its first two decades and was succeeded by [[Andrew Sutherland (mathematician)|Andrew Sutherland]] in 2019.{{r|ntf}}{{r|jmm}}
